'''Francis Sowerby Macaulay''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Baker | first1 = H. F. | title = Francis Sowerby Macaulay. 1862-1937 | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1938.0018  | doi-access = free| journal = [[Obituary Notices of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 2 | issue = 6 | pages = 356–361| year = 1938 }}</ref> (11 February 1862, [[Witney]] – 9 February 1937, [[Cambridge]]) was an [[England|English]] mathematician who made significant contributions to [[algebraic geometry]].<ref>{{MacTutor Biography|id=Macaulay}}</ref> He is known for his 1916 book ''The Algebraic Theory of Modular Systems'' (an old term for [[Ideal (ring theory)|ideals]]), which greatly influenced the later course of [[commutative algebra]]. [[Cohen–Macaulay ring]]s, [[Macaulay duality]], the [[Macaulay resultant]] and the [[Macaulay computer algebra system|Macaulay]] and [[Macaulay2]] [[computer algebra system]]s are named for Macaulay.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Eisenbud |first1=David |author-link=David Eisenbud |last2=Gray |first2=Jeremy |author-link2=Jeremy Gray (mathematician) |date=2023 |title=F. S. Macaulay: From plane curves to Gorenstein rings |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2023-60-03/S0273-0979-2023-01787-4/S0273-0979-2023-01787-4.pdf |journal=[[Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.]] |volume=60 |issue= 3|pages=371–406 |doi=10.1090/bull/1787 |access-date=}}</ref>

Macaulay was educated at [[Kingswood School]] and graduated with distinction from [[St John's College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{acad|id=FML879FS|name=Macaulay, Francis Sowerby}}</ref> He taught the top mathematics class in [[St Paul's School (London)|St Paul's School]] in [[London]] from 1885 to 1911.  His students included [[John Edensor Littlewood|J. E. Littlewood]] and [[G. N. Watson]].

In 1928 Macaulay was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref name="frs"/>
